skills/make-it-so/playbooks/orchestrate..why: The orch CLI is excluded and the verification ledger lives in GitHub: every orch command becomes a direct store-file edit or a ledger comment on the PR, the store moves to ~/.claude/projects/<project>/, and restacks and cloud-only spawns become background agents with worktree isolation. The orch frontier command's empty-gt guard becomes an instruction. Worktree agents share one repository, so workers release their branches and the lander frees held branches before a rebase. Every agent runs on this machine, so the isolation exception covers only the coordinator's own working tree and worktree agents may read the store. The different-family verifier resolves to the models document's verifier and verifier-diff-audit roles, with a fallback line when there is no second family. Kitchen: every landing passes Autopilot-full's merge gate, and a closed gate parks in gates.md for the chef; human-in-the-loop units become local Projects threads running the grilling skill, which picks its own channel; a marker sentence says the Projects coordinator plus routines replace the /loop wakes and points at the Projects kit (the coordinator brief and routine prompts) in skills/setup-milliways/projects/. Reflect: ends with the Reflect step every make-it-so playbook ends with, which files a garden issue for each thing the thread worked around (spec #66). No stacks (spec #66 story 42): Stack safety becomes Merge safety, where each unit is one PR off trunk, dependent units are merge-then-branch, the frontier is recomputed with gh instead of gt, and one lander replaces the stacker. Audit fixes (#77 audit): in a Claude Project the coordinator brief replaces this playbook and the project conversation does not route through make-it-so; the standing-orders register is standing-orders.md, the brief's name; the ledger paragraph points at docs/agents/verification.md, its one full statement; the retro watcher becomes the post-merge sweep, which files issues (garden for workarounds); a prototype pick leaves the human-in-the-loop list, since its one channel is the draft prototype: PR, and a drain that finds the pick spawns the unit that finishes it. Round 2 (#77 audit): the done predicate counts units merged with their ledger tier recorded; a unit verified by one cheap command gets its receipt recorded as unit-test-verified or type-check-only, which never passes the gate, so it waits for the chef's merge, and the cheap-unit pilot fans out once its receipt is in the ledger. The merge gate binds every merge except the chef's own; landing names units whose gate holds rather than verified units; the cheap pilot's path ends at its merge-ready stop. Local threads run on the chef's own machine, not a Mac by name. Verifier (#109): a unit's verifier and a completion that needs review point at Who verifies in docs/agents/verification.md instead of restating it. Output directories (#105): each worker and verifier gets its own output directory named in its brief, and the brief's SCOPE field names it, pointing at make-it-so's Subagents section.

skills/make-it-so/SKILL.md.why: Router: renamed make-it-so and made the kitchen's entry point, reached through the root AGENTS.md line, so the sticky-mode frontmatter (mode, icon, color, reminder) goes and the description says when to route. Routing rule: running something can answer it -> prototype; a one-way door or taste, intent or domain words only the chef holds -> grill with the grilling skill, which picks its own channel (browser or text); bigger than one context -> wayfinder; human-in-the-loop work runs as a local Projects thread with a plain-text fallback. Overlap wiring: Matt's implement, tdd, diagnosing-bugs, code-review, prototype and grilling are the procedures for their jobs; tdd-bug-fix stays for bugs, interrogate for one-way doors, and the Spec and tickets playbook is listed. Every playbook ends with Reflect. No stacks: Autopilot-stack is not listed (its playbook is deleted), and Orchestrate and multi-phase plans no longer say stacked PRs. Autonomy: merges follow the trust ladder's merge gate, and one-way doors always wait for the chef. Model-invocable: milliways:sous-chef preloads it, and Claude Code cannot preload a skill with model invocation off. Roles: the Subagents defaults resolve from docs/agents/models.md (written by setup-milliways) instead of setup-pstack and Cursor model slugs. Leaf skills: says where principle leaves and this skill's own files live (<milliways>), since Claude Code does not list skills with model invocation off. Audit fixes (#77 audit): the Subagents section states the delegation base case (a step's subagent executes the step and does not re-route or spawn unless briefed to); the Playbooks preamble orders large work (wayfinder, then Spec and tickets, then Multi-phase plan run by Autopilot-full with the plan as GitHub tickets in a Claude Project, then figure-it-out, then Autonomous run); a chef's explicit merge request is the chef's own merge, recorded in the ledger comment, and every other merge, Shipping's and Babysit's included, goes through the merge gate; Shipping and Babysit take one PR or a queue of independent PRs; in a Claude Project the coordinator brief replaces Orchestrate; a prototype pick's one channel is its draft prototype: PR, so it leaves the human-in-the-loop list; Opening a PR ends every playbook that ships a change; on-ramps suggest /triage and /improve-codebase-architecture to the chef, send codebase upkeep to the garden loop, and send a spec to build to Spec and tickets' hand-off. The sequence-verifiable-units entry says order commits and PRs, not stack them. Round 2 (#77 audit): the Shipping line and the trust-ladder paragraph point at docs/agents/verification.md for the chef's own merge, which holds whatever the PR's tier, and every other merge goes through the gate; in a Claude Project a multi-phase plan's published parent issue is the plan. The chef's own merge covers merge, land or ship. Local threads run on the chef's own machine, not a Mac by name. No phantom steps (#108): a Non-negotiables paragraph says a checklist line never claims work that didn't run, so each step is done with its evidence or marked skip: <reason>; the Subagents defaults say a brief that hands off a skill says "read <path> in full before starting", not "see <path>". Subagent isolation (#104, #105): the Subagents section says nothing writable is shared between subagents. One that writes repository files or changes the working tree runs with worktree isolation (one that needs the thread's own working tree runs with no other writer), each gets its own scratchpad output directory named in its brief, and the thread keeps its drafts in a directory no subagent is given. Wayfinder tickets: the Routing rule's first entry sends a wayfinder map or a wayfinder:* issue to the wayfinder skill's Work through the map mode, because a single ticket fits one session and so never matched the bigger-than-one-context entry, and the per-type rules below it skipped the claim, resolution comment, close and map update.
